extraction.name: MINT-1T
extraction.description: MINT-1T (Multimodal INTerleaved) is the largest and most diverse open-source multimodal interleaved dataset to date, comprising one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images sourced from HTML documents, PDFs, and ArXiv papers. It represents a 10x scale-up from existing open-source datasets and is designed for pre-training large multimodal models that can process multiple interleaved images and text.
extraction.creator: University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, University of California Berkeley
extraction.publisher: University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, University of California Berkeley
extraction.citeAs: Awadalla, Anas, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, and Ludwig Schmidt. 'MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens.' arXiv:2406.11271v5 [cs.CV], 31 Oct 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MINT-1T curates large-scale open-source multimodal interleaved documents from three sources: (1) HTML documents extracted from CommonCrawl WARC files by parsing each WARC entry's DOM tree, covering May 2017 to April 2024 dumps; (2) PDF documents sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files from February 2023 to April 2024 dumps, downloaded and parsed using PyMuPDF; (3) ArXiv interleaved documents built from LaTeX source code using TexSoup to find figure tags and interleave images with paper text. The data was collected from January 2024 to June 2024 and includes web data from 2013 to 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For HTML documents, any non-retrievable image links are discarded and documents with no valid image links are removed. PDF documents that are more than 50MB or over 50 pages long are discarded. Pages containing no text are excluded. Some images cannot be detected due to limitations of the PyMuPDF package.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: HTML documents from CommonCrawl WARC files (May 2017 to April 2024), PDF documents from CommonCrawl WAT files (February 2023 to April 2024), and ArXiv documents from ArXiv LaTeX source code (via ArXiv S3 buckets). The final dataset contains 922 billion HTML tokens, 93 billion PDF tokens, and 9 billion ArXiv tokens.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data collection was conducted from January 2024 to June 2024. Web data spans from 2013 to 2024. HTML documents cover CommonCrawl dumps from May 2017 to April 2024. PDF documents cover CommonCrawl WAT files from February 2023 to April 2024.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For PDF documents, reading order is obtained by finding the bounding box of all text blocks on a page, clustering the blocks based on columns, and ordering the blocks from top left to bottom right. Images are anchored in the sequence based on proximity between the image's bounding box and text blocks on the same page. For ArXiv, multi-file papers are handled by identifying the main Tex file and replacing input tags with the contents of its file. LaTeX code is cleaned by removing imports, bibliography, tables, and citation tags. Email addresses are replaced with templates such as 'email@example.com' and IP addresses are replaced with randomly generated non-functional IPs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text Quality Filtering: Non-English documents are eliminated using Fasttext's language identification model (confidence threshold 0.65). Documents with URLs containing NSFW substrings are removed. Text filtering methods from RefinedWeb are applied, removing documents with excessive duplicate n-grams or those identified as low quality using MassiveText rules. Image Filtering: Images smaller than 150 pixels or larger than 20,000 pixels are removed. For HTML, images with aspect ratio greater than two are removed; for PDFs, the threshold is three. NSFW Image Filtering: An NSFW image detector is applied; documents containing a single NSFW image are discarded entirely. Deduplication: Bloom Filter-based paragraph and document deduplication with false positive rate 0.01, deduplicating 13-gram paragraphs; documents where more than 80% of paragraphs are duplicates are discarded. Common boilerplate text is removed via exact paragraph deduplication on 2% of each CommonCrawl snapshot. Image deduplication is performed using SHA256 hashes, removing images appearing more than ten times within a snapshot and removing repeated images within a single document.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Fasttext language identification model (for non-English document filtering), NSFW image detector (https://github.com/GantMan/nsfw_model), PyMuPDF (for PDF parsing), TexSoup (for ArXiv LaTeX parsing), Bloom Filter via BFF (https://github.com/allenai/bff) for deduplication, datatrove (https://github.com/huggingface/datatrove) for text quality filters, OBELICS HTML parser (https://github.com/huggingface/OBELICS), GPT-4 (for domain classification in analysis), LDA model (for topic modeling in diversity analysis)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released to the public through the Huggingface interface as JSON shards. The authors of this work will actively respond to issues and maintain the dataset. Updates will be communicated through the README in the Huggingface interface. An erratum will be present on the README of the Huggingface dataset page. Older versions can be found using the Git history of the dataset repository. Contributions can be made through the Pull Request mechanism of the Huggingface interface. A Google form will be provided to allow removal of samples from MINT-1T. The dataset was planned for release in July 2024.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset may contain images of individuals and text about specific individuals present on the public web. It may also contain sensitive data such as race or ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions, financial or health data, or other sensitive information present on the public web. Email addresses and IP addresses are masked to mitigate personal data leakage. The dataset does not explicitly identify subpopulations but such information may be extractable.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MINT-1T is intended to make research into large multimodal models more accessible by providing a large-scale open-source dataset. The authors note that future work should explore more ways to improve the safety of multimodal internet data. Using the dataset to train models that ingest or generate personally identifying information (such as images of people's faces and other sensitive content) as well as military applications are considered inappropriate use cases.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: OBELICS, a predecessor dataset, shows a pronounced concentration in 'Humanities and Social Sciences' due to its filtering process that favors Wikipedia-like articles. MINT-1T's HTML subset is not strongly biased towards any specific domain. The PDF subset has a higher proportion of 'Science and Technology' documents. The authors note they avoid using text quality classifier models as they have been shown to favor text from certain demographics. The dataset may contain biases present in web-crawled data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MINT-1T is not self-contained and relies on downloading external image URLs, with no guarantees these URLs will remain available over time due to link rot. The dataset is over 300TB, making it infeasible to host the full dataset with images. PDF parsing using PyMuPDF has two noted limitations: (1) sometimes unable to detect images, and (2) incorrect reading order extraction due to arbitrary PDF layouts (e.g., incorrectly reading across column boundaries). The dataset may contain confidential, offensive, or sensitive content despite filtering efforts. The dataset should not be used for training models that ingest or generate personally identifying information or for military applications.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use case is pre-training large multimodal models (LMMs) that can process multiple interleaved images and text sequences. The dataset is designated as a research artifact. Other potential uses include generating interleaved images and text sequences and building multimodal document retrieval systems. There is only a training split for MINT-1T.
